title: Why AI Agents Need Million-Token Context — Thomas Wolf & Olive Song, MiniMax
talk_summary: Interview with MiniMax's Olive Song about M3: 1M-token sparse attention, native multimodality, and internal research culture. Most content is model-lab strategy; only a few mechanisms transfer to agent orchestration, mainly long-context handling, routing, and automated harnesses.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue agentic tasks need long context because the model must see environment and tool responses across many rounds; shorter context loses task state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: getting all the tool responses, getting multi rounds the like shorter context wouldn't be enough to perform the complex task

takeaways.technique: Route by task complexity and context length
takeaways.what_they_do: They highlight model routing and multi-agent setups to handle more complex tasks and reveal model capability boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: model routing, multi-agents um that allows even more capabilities, even more complex tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: After releases, team members play with the model, find weaknesses, and propose projects; others join if interested.
takeaways.evidence_quote: find their own weaknesses and propose a thing that they want to improve on the model

takeaways.what_they_do: They build internal research harnesses to automate workflows and iterate faster.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we build our own research harnesses that automate our workflows

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe using multimodal models to read unstructured reports or long video and then act with tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: read a PP- PowerPoint, uh or to read some report that is not very structured
